acv.quote: We proposed six hundred K a year.

header.reason: Angela, the COO who signed with Adyen, was deciding on the stores: returns at the till, who does the installs, and a credible rollout plan. We described all of that and never showed it. The rep frames it as a win on the web side that Raj (the CTO) backed, but nothing in the transcript shows any business coming to us, and Raj did not make the final call.

findings.finding: We sold to the CTO who ran the RFP, while the COO who signed was met only once, so store-led deals need the operations executive engaged early and directly.

Answering 'who does the installs' with 'a partner' ended store operations' interest, because the COO wanted one accountable vendor; we need a credible rollout story that includes installs, dates and old tills.
findings.quote: I don't want two vendors pointing at each other.

findings.finding: Store operations asked to see an online order returned at a till, live, and we only described it; that return is the demo for retail deals, and a slide got called 'a diagram'.
findings.quote: We described it. We never showed it.

findings.finding: The customer talked about 'the tills' and one system, while we said 'unified commerce', 'in-person payments' and 'point of sale'; our store messaging should use their plain words.
findings.quote: One system for the tills and the website.
findings.who: Bev (head of store operations), relayed by Tom

findings.finding: According to Raj, Adyen brought a retail team and named retailers the COO knew, while we sent a case study and couldn't arrange the reference call she asked for; we need retail references ready to call.
findings.quote: we couldn't set up a call in time.
